q: Name the vulnerability in Android devices that caught the eye of the cyber security wing of India's Ministry of Home Affairs in December 2019.
explanation: StrandHogg is the Android vulnerability that MHA's cyber wing (I4C Threat Analytical Unit) flagged to the States in December 2019: it lets malicious apps pose as genuine apps and steal data. Trojan Horse, the Morris Worm (1988) and Timofonica (2000) are older malware.

options: Issuing alerts and advisories regarding the latest cyber threats and countermeasures on a regular basis
Managing the cyber security budget for private companies
Providing legal support for cybercrime investigations
key_text: Issuing alerts and advisories regarding the latest cyber threats and countermeasures on a regular basis
explanation: CERT-In identifies cyber incidents and issues alerts and advisories on the latest cyber threats and countermeasures, reported daily. Treaties, private security budgets and legal support for cybercrime cases are not its functions.

notes.text: - **Features:** **compliance**, **defence against internal threats**, **threat prevention** – so "all of the above".

q: Which Indian agency is responsible for Cyber Security?
explanation: CERT-In, under MeitY since January 2004, is the national agency for cyber security and cyber incident response. RAW is foreign intelligence, ISRO is space and NITI Aayog is a policy think tank.

notes.text: - **Cyber security:** protecting computer-based information from unauthorised access, transfer, modification or destruction; threats = hacking, malware, cybercrime, cyber terrorism, data theft.

exam: APPSC AEE General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
q: In 2017, The Supreme Court of India ruled that Right to Privacy is 'intrinsic to life and personal liberty' and is inherently protected under ____, and as a part of the freedom guaranteed by Part III of the Constitution.
explanation: In K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017) the Supreme Court held privacy protected as an intrinsic part of life and personal liberty under Article 21 and as part of the freedoms of Part III. Articles 20, 22 and 23 deal with conviction, detention and forced labour.

notes.text: - **Decided 24 Aug 2017** by a **9-judge** bench, **unanimous**: right to privacy is **intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21** and part of the freedoms of **Part III** – a **Fundamental Right**.
